facts.P1_fx_receipts: Yes; up to $20,000 can arrive without a formal declaration.
facts.P2_fcy_account: Yes: keep up to 50% of earnings in an ERQ foreign-currency account (ICT freelancers).
facts.P3_local_gateways: SSLCOMMERZ onboards sole proprietors and Facebook sellers; it asks for TIN or NID.
facts.L1_registration: No company needed, but online sellers must hold an ID like a TIN.
facts.L2_tax_id: TIN (e-TIN), registered online with the NBR using your National ID.
facts.L3_income_tax_foreign: Freelancing and content creation income is tax-free until June 2027 if paid through banks.
facts.L4_vat_gst: 15% VAT; registration needed only above BDT 5 million turnover a year.
facts.L5_data_protection: Personal Data Protection Act 2026; you need explicit consent to collect data.
facts.L6_consumer_ecommerce: Show your ID number, full terms and refund rules on your sales page.
facts.L7_incentives: Freelance income is tax-free until June 2027; keep up to 50% in dollars.

watch_out.text: The tax exemption needs all business money to move through bank transfer.
Payment gateways (OPGSPs) can bring in at most US$10,000 per transaction.
Selling online without a TIN or trade licence breaks the digital commerce rules.
